matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: Compute the integer values of both sides (including any arithmetic) to determine the numeric imbalance, then search for a single‑stick move that changes a numeral or operator by exactly that amount, making the equation balanced.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the equation is false and you have the full set of numerals and operators available.
matchstick.example: Assuming a difference of 5 but moving a stick that only changes a value by 1, leaving the equation still false.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and a V appears on the side that must increase, reposition one of the V’s diagonal sticks so that the two sticks cross, turning the V into an X (value +5).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the side needing increase contains a V and the numeric imbalance is 5.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from V to make an I, which reduces the value instead of increasing it.

matchstick.title: Change + to - and add I
matchstick.principle: Remove the vertical stick from a plus sign to turn it into a minus sign (changing + B to – B, decreasing the side by 2·value(B)), then place that stick as a new I in a numeral, increasing the other side by 1; net effect is –1, useful when the imbalance is 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a plus sign is present, the imbalance is 1 (or –1), and there is a numeral that can accept an extra I without breaking Roman rules.
matchstick.example: Changing + to – but forgetting to add the removed stick as an I, so the total change is –2 instead of –1.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Move a vertical I‑stick from any numeral that contains at least one I to another numeral that can legally gain an I, adjusting the values by ±1 on each side.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is 1 (or –1) and both a source numeral with an extra I and a destination numeral that can accept an I exist.
matchstick.example: Taking the only I from a solitary I, which would delete the numeral entirely.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If both a minus sign (single horizontal stick) and an equals sign (two horizontals) appear, move one horizontal stick from the equals sign to the minus sign; the minus becomes an equals and the original equals becomes a minus, preserving total sticks and potentially fixing the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is false and swapping the positions of ‘‑’ and ‘=’ could resolve the numeric imbalance.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from ‘=’ and leaving only one horizontal line, which is not a valid equality sign.

matchstick.title: Ensure a valid '=' remains when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: The equality sign must consist of two horizontal sticks; if you take a stick away, you must either replace it elsewhere to keep a valid '=', or convert the sign into another valid operator as part of a planned transformation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any time you consider moving a stick from the equals sign.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal line from '=', leaving a single line that no longer represents equality.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and an X appears on the side that must decrease, reposition one of the X’s diagonal sticks so that the sticks no longer cross, turning the X into a V (value –5).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the side needing decrease contains an X and the numeric imbalance is 5.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from X and discarding it, which would leave an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Evaluate expressions when computing numeric imbalance
matchstick.principle: Before comparing the two sides, fully evaluate any arithmetic expressions (e.g., ‘XI + I’) to obtain their integer values; the imbalance is the difference between these totals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any puzzle where the sides contain ‘+’ or ‘‑’ operators.
matchstick.example: Comparing raw Roman numerals without performing the addition/subtraction, leading to a wrong imbalance.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick across equality
matchstick.principle: When the numeric imbalance is exactly 2, move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral on the side with excess to a numeral on the other side, decreasing one side by 1 and increasing the other by 1, thereby fixing the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by 2 and both sides contain a numeral that can lose/gain an I.
matchstick.example: Moving an I from a solitary I on the larger side, which would delete that numeral.

matchstick.title: Reposition I before X to change XI to IX
matchstick.principle: If a numeral ‘XI’ appears, moving its I‑stick to the left of the X changes it to ‘IX’, decreasing the value by 2.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is 2 and a ‘XI’ is present on the side that needs to decrease.
matchstick.example: Moving the I from ‘XI’ to another numeral without placing it before the X, resulting in an invalid numeral.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I).
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any numeral can donate a stick, ignoring the structural requirement that some numerals need all their sticks to remain a valid symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only move a stick from a numeral that still forms a valid Roman numeral after the removal; check that the source numeral still matches a legal pattern.

matchstick.description: Providing an invalid equation after moving a stick (including incomplete or unreachable solutions).
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on moving a stick but does not verify that the resulting symbols form a syntactically correct Roman numeral equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each proposed move, re‑parse the entire equation to ensure every numeral and operator is valid and the expression is well‑formed.

matchstick.description: Changing – to + without adding the required vertical stick.
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats the plus sign as a single stick, forgetting that a plus sign consists of both a vertical and a horizontal stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Remember that turning a minus into a plus requires adding a vertical stick; you must source that stick from somewhere else.

matchstick.description: Using an angled stick as a vertical stick (or vice versa).
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model ignores the orientation of sticks, treating any stick as interchangeable regardless of angle.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Respect stick orientation: only vertical sticks can become I, and only diagonal sticks can form V or X; do not repurpose an angled stick as a vertical one.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign and leaving no valid '=' sign in the equation.
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a horizontal line from '=', not realizing that '=' must retain two horizontals to stay a valid equality sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never remove a stick from '=', unless you simultaneously transform the sign into another valid operator (e.g., minus) as part of a planned swap.
